newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude grades resist outright price collapse.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude grades resist outright price collapse.

text.p: U.S. domestic crudes resisted the day's outright price collapse, aided by refiner demand for light crudes in a tight environment, traders said Thursday.
News a U.S. brokered ceasefire had been extended between Iraq's rival Kurdish factions, renewing hope for an Iraq oil sale, triggered massive selling in NYMEX futures.
But near-term fundamentals still pointed to a shortage of domestic distillate-rich crudes from a lack of arbitrage due to a narrow Brent/West Texas Intermediate spread at 50-55 cts.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $23.20-30 a barrel, down about $1.15 from Wednesday.
Outright prices staged a rapid and sustained decline spurred by liquidation in both crude and products, with the Dec/Jan WTI spread drifting to 30 cents from 38 cents.
This pushed WTI/Cushing Posting Plus to a low of postings plus $2.03 from $2.11 a barrel. Jan grades were traded a few times at postings plus $2.07 a barrel, on short covering.
Domestic crudes stayed mostly grounded, and recouped some bullish momentum in late activity.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St James traded at WTI plus 73-75 cents, up from from 65-68 cents, while Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire rebounded to plus 75-78 cents from 70 cents.
Midland/WTI moved at plus 5 cents, unchanged from the previous day, while West Texas Sour/Midland improved modestly to a discount of $1.47 a barrel, up two cents.
The U.S. government's sale of $1.9 million barrels of sour crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) had only a scant bearish impact on sours, traders said.
Inland WTS reacted less than Eugene Island, which eased to minus $1.14 a barrel versus $1.12 on Wednesday.
